column2: Interactive module for the Foundation Engineering course at the BME Faculty of Civil Engineering (Department of Engineering Geology and Geotechnics). The numerical examples and simulators are simplified models for teaching purposes.

Illustrative model: 6 m thick normally consolidated clay, σ′<sub>0</sub> = 60 kPa, C<sub>c</sub> = 0.45, C<sub>r</sub> = 0.06, e<sub>0</sub> = 1.2. If Δσ ≤ Δσ<sub>p</sub>, the soil below the building compresses only along the reloading branch (with a small slope).
σ<sub>2</sub> = P / (B + 2·v·tanϑ) + γ<sub>1</sub>·v, where γ<sub>1</sub> = 20 kN/m³ is the unit weight of the replacement soil – simplified illustration.

Did you know? The 44-storey Torre Latinoamericana in Mexico City (1956), 182 m high including its antenna, stands on extremely compressible volcanic clay: its base slab is 13.5 m deep, and the load is carried by 361 piles down to a dense sand layer 33 m deep. Its structural and foundation designer, Leonardo Zeevaert, also exploited the weight of the excavated soil – the tower “does not settle, it floats”, and it withstood the magnitude 7.9 earthquake of 1957.
A strip footing deeper than 2–2.5 m is no longer economical – in that case pad foundations (or caisson foundations) are advisable, tied together at the top by a grid of ground beams.

The simulator follows the steps of the more accurate settlement calculation: permanent load → stress below the footing (below the centre of a rectangular loaded area, Steinbrenner; or Jáky’s linear approximation) → influence depth (Jáky: m<sub>0</sub> = B for a square footing; or the 0.2·σ<sub>0</sub> criterion of Hungarian practice) → summation by layer: s = Σ Δσ<sub>z</sub>·Δh / E<sub>oed</sub>. The effect of excavation is taken into account through the net pressure q<sub>0</sub> = q − γ·D; the weight of the footing and the backfill is added to the load. A teaching model, not design software.
Partly compensated: ${pct(pc)} of the load is “counterbalanced” by the excavated soil – settlement arises only from the excess, and starts only when construction exceeds the unloading.

The foundation level is on the gravel – the settlement is a fraction of the initial value. Remember: a strip footing deeper than 2–2.5 m is no longer economical → pad footings with ground beams, caisson foundations or a basement.

Deeper foundation level: below the soft layer there is gravel from 2.6 m. Take the foundation level down! Deepening by +0.5 m: ${pc(dD)}. When the foundation level reaches the gravel, the settlement drops to a fraction.

Homogeneous soil: widening reduces the settlement, but not proportionally – the wider foundation is heavier, and the stress reaches deeper below it. Widening by +0.5 m: ${pc(dB)}; deepening by +0.5 m: ${pc(dD)}.

Case B: widening hardly helps (+0.5 m: ${pc(dB)}), because under the wider foundation the stresses reach deeper, and the soft clay lower down takes the load. ${st.method === 'E' ? 'Válts Jáky-módszerre: ott a süllyedés még nő is!' : ''}
